title: 証城寺の狸囃子 (Shōjōji no Tanuki Bayashi — The Raccoon Drum-Dance of Shojoji)
description: A playful 1925 children's song about tanuki (raccoon dogs) belly-drumming in the moonlit garden of Shojoji temple. The tanuki call out to each other (皆出て来い) to beat their bellies together (ぽんぽこぽんのぽん) and challenge the temple's head priest to a drum-off. Based on an old legend from Kisarazu, Chiba, the song captures the mischievous spirit of tanuki folklore and is one of Japan's most beloved children's songs.
